summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would appropriate money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the ordinary annual services of the Government, adding to the 2024-25 Budget appropriations to fund decisions made since the Budget.

It would fund the amounts in Schedule 1 as departmental items, administered items tied to outcomes and corporate entity items, which the relevant Department pays to corporate Commonwealth entities and companies.

It sits with Appropriation Bill (No. 4) and the Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 2) 2024-2025 as the Additional Estimates Appropriation Bills, would commence on Royal Assent and would be repealed on 1 July 2027.
changes: Departmental items could be applied to any payment related to a non-corporate entity's functions, including employee and supplier costs and minor assets valued at $10 million or less.
Administered amounts would be appropriated separately for each outcome, with the portfolio statements determining which activities count towards an outcome.
The Advance to the Finance Minister would be restored to its original $400 million once the bill commences, and any advance already allocated for the same expenditure would reduce the appropriation.
Notional transactions between non-corporate Commonwealth entities would be treated as real and would debit the appropriation.
Amounts could be credited to a special account where an item shares the account's purpose, and the Portfolio Additional Estimates Statements would be relevant documents for interpreting the Act.
summary.affected: Non-corporate Commonwealth entities, corporate Commonwealth entities and Commonwealth companies that receive appropriations, and the Finance Minister are affected.

speeches.speaker: Luke Howarth
speeches.brief: Supported additional appropriation bills providing $12 billion for the remainder of the financial year, including $7 billion for ordinary annual services, while arguing that government economic management had worsened inflation, living costs, energy prices and business conditions; debate was interrupted.

speeches.speaker: Katy Gallagher
speeches.brief: Moved procedural motions to suspend standing orders, allow immediate consideration of legislation, limit debate on specified bills, and set the Senate's hours and adjournment arrangements.
